title: Time-versioned key-value store
prompt:
Design a key-value store that keeps every version of each key, so you can ask what value a key had at any past timestamp.

- Implement the class VersionedStore with set(key, value, t) and get(key, t). The driver runVersionedStore(ops) is already written: ops looks like [["set", "a", "x", 5], ["get", "a", 7]] and it returns one output per op (null/None for "set").
- get(key, t) returns the value from the set of that key with the largest timestamp <= t, or "" (empty string) if there is none (including keys never set).
- For any single key, set timestamps strictly increase from one call to the next. get timestamps can be anything from 0 to 10^9, in any order.
- Keys and values are non-empty strings; up to 100,000 ops. Aim for O(1) per set and O(log n) per get.
hints: For one key, the set timestamps arrive already sorted. What does that let you do at query time?
Store, per key, a list of (timestamp, value) pairs in the order they were set, and binary-search it in get.
Find the first timestamp strictly greater than t (upper bound). If its index is 0 return "", otherwise return the value at index - 1.

solution.explanation: Each key keeps parallel lists of timestamps and values; because set timestamps per key strictly increase, appending keeps the timestamp list sorted. get binary-searches for the first timestamp greater than t, and the version just before it is the answer (or "" if there is none).

complexity.time: O(1) per set, O(log v) per get
complexity.notes: v is the number of versions of the queried key and n the total number of sets. If timestamps could arrive out of order you would need a balanced tree or sorted insertion instead of append.

followUps: Support delete(key, t) so that gets at or after t return "" until the next set.
How would you cap memory by keeping only the last m versions of each key?
